module

public import Mathlib.Algebra.MvPolynomial.CommRing
public import Mathlib.RingTheory.Localization.FractionRing

@[expose] public section

/-- The field of multivariate rational functions in variables indexed by `σ` over a commutative
ring `K`, defined as the fraction field of the multivariate polynomial ring `MvPolynomial σ K`. -/
abbrev MvRatFunc (σ K : Type*) [CommRing K] := FractionRing (MvPolynomial σ K)

/--
A rational function $g$ is defined at a point $x_0$ if $g$ can be written as $p / q$
where $p, q$ are polynomials and $q(x_0) \neq 0$.
-/
def IsDefined (σ K : Type*) [CommRing K] [IsDomain K] (g : MvRatFunc σ K) (x₀ : σ → K) : Prop :=
  ∃ p q : MvPolynomial σ K, g = (algebraMap _ _ p) / (algebraMap _ _ q) ∧ q.eval x₀ ≠ 0

findings.description: The docstring calls this a field over an arbitrary commutative ring, but the declaration assumes only `[CommRing K]`. `FractionRing` then constructs the total fraction ring, which need not be a field. Lean tests exhibit nonzero elements with product zero in `MvRatFunc Unit (ZMod 6)`, and prove `0 = 1` for `MvRatFunc Unit (ZMod 1)`. The construction itself follows Mathlib's convention, and both current problem use sites have field coefficients; the issue is the unconditional field claim in the documentation.
findings.source_evidence: Mathlib/RingTheory/Localization/FractionRing.lean explicitly describes the CommRing-general construction as the 'total fraction ring'; its field instance requires an integral domain. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Field_of_fractions likewise distinguishes total quotient rings from fraction fields.
findings.suggested_fix: Describe this as the total fraction ring of `MvPolynomial σ K`, adding that it is a field when `[IsDomain K]`. The abbreviation need not be restricted.

findings.description: In FormalConjectures/LittProblems/1.lean:60–66, `IsDefined g (constantCoeff ∘ pt)` supplies some suitable representation of g, but does not ensure that the separately chosen denominator q used in the cleared ODE remains nonzero after substitution. The condition `q ≠ 0` only concerns the polynomial. Lean proves `IsSolutionOfAlgebraicODE 1 (0 : PowerSeries ℚ) 1`: choose p = q = `MvPolynomial.X 1`, which is nonzero but evaluates to zero on (z,0). The cleared equation becomes 0 = 0, while IsDefined uses 1 = 1/1. Nevertheless the intended equation f' = 1 is false for f = 0. A scratch proof also establishes non-equivalence with the repaired predicate. The library's IsDefined definition is correct; this is a misuse at its problem-file use site.
findings.source_evidence: Lam–Litt, arXiv:2501.13175v1, §1.1, equation (1.1) and its footnote require f^(n)(z) = g(z,f,…,f^(n−1)), with g represented by p/q having q(0,t₀,…,tₙ₋₁) ≠ 0. https://www.problemsilike.com/1 requires the same nonsingular solution condition.
findings.suggested_fix: Require `q.eval (PowerSeries.constantCoeff ∘ pt) ≠ 0` for the SAME existential q used in the representation and cleared ODE. This can replace `q ≠ 0` and the independent IsDefined conjunct, both of which then follow. The substituted denominator is consequently a unit in ℚ[[z]], making denominator clearing valid.

findings.description: FormalConjectures/LittProblems/1.lean:155–158 inherits the incorrect ODE predicate and admits the source's explicitly excluded singular counterexample H(z) = Σₘ binom(2m,m)² z^m/16^m. It is nonalgebraic and has coefficients in ℤ[1/16]. Its relation z(1−z)H'' + (1−2z)H' − H/4 = 0 makes the current hODE hold with n = 3, g = 0, numerator 0, and denominator Q = z(1−z)Y₂ + (1−2z)Y₁ − Y₀/4. Q is a nonzero polynomial, but its substitution is zero, so the alleged ODE equation is vacuous. Thus the theorem has a false instance, unlike the source's requirement to solve the specified nonsingular ODE. Lean verifies Q ≠ 0 and acceptance of every series satisfying this relation.
findings.source_evidence: https://www.problemsilike.com/1 explicitly gives this hypergeometric series as a counterexample if nonsingularity is omitted. Lam–Litt, https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.13175, Remark 1.1.3, calls it nonalgebraic with only powers of 2 in its Taylor denominators, and explains that it is excluded because the ODE is singular at 0. The paper also supplies the hypergeometric differential operator from which the displayed relation follows.
findings.suggested_fix: Repair `LamLitt.IsSolutionOfAlgebraicODE` by requiring nonvanishing at the initial point of the actual denominator used in the cleared equation. Retain the conjecture's open status: this counterexample concerns the formalization, not the source conjecture.

findings.description: FormalConjectures/LittProblems/1.lean:144–147 inherits the same denominator-witness defect. Its actual (3) ⇒ (2) statement consequently covers arbitrary differentially algebraic series, not just solutions of the specified nonsingular ODE. For example, F(z) = Σₘ≥1 z^(m²)/m² satisfies omega-integrality with ω(p) = p²−1, but has no finite set of denominator primes; these arithmetic assertions are proved in the scratch files. F is differentially algebraic: zF' = (θ₃(z)−1)/2, the theta/eta identity expresses θ₃ through Euler products at z,z²,z⁴, and Ramanujan's differential identities put all derivatives of F in a differential field generated by 13 elements over ℚ(z). Hence a nonzero polynomial Q(z,F,…,F^(13)) vanishes. Choosing n = 14, g = 0, numerator 0 and denominator Q satisfies the current hODE, giving a false instance of the integrality conclusion. The differential-field argument is detailed in review_notes.md; that part is not formalized in Lean.
findings.source_evidence: Lam–Litt, arXiv:2501.13175v1, §1.1 and Conjecture 1.1.1, impose the nonsingular ODE condition before asserting the three-way equivalence. The counterexample's differential algebraicity follows from the displayed identities in https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theta_function#Relations_to_Dedekind_eta_function, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dedekind_eta_function, and https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eisenstein_series#Ramanujan_identities.
findings.suggested_fix: Use the corrected `IsSolutionOfAlgebraicODE` requiring the chosen denominator to be nonzero at the initial point. The same shared-definition repair fixes both Lam–Litt implications.

reformulations.difference: The conclusion uses algebraicity over `Polynomial ℚ`, whereas the paper says algebraicity over ℚ(z). This aspect is correct independently of the ODE defect.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Embed ℚ[[z]] injectively into its fraction field. Algebraicity is preserved and reflected by this embedding. Algebraicity over ℚ[z] is then equivalent to algebraicity over its fraction field ℚ(z), by clearing coefficient denominators. The exact equivalence after this embedding is proved in /workspace/review/equivalences.lean using Mathlib's `isAlgebraic_algebraMap_iff` and `IsFractionRing.isAlgebraic_iff`.

reformulations.difference: The parameter N ranges over all natural numbers, including 0, whereas Litt's website specifies a positive integer N. This boundary convention is harmless.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Here `ℤAdjoinInvNat 0 = Algebra.adjoin ℤ {0} = ℤAdjoinInvNat 1`: both are the embedded integers. Any witness N = 0 can therefore be replaced by N = 1 without changing the coefficient condition. The equivalence between unrestricted and positive-N existence is proved in /workspace/review/equivalences.lean.

Left both definitions unchanged. The three substantive findings cannot be fixed within the allowed file. The required compile command completed without errors or warnings.
